response.query: Can local labs perform required biomarker assays (DBS CRP, HemoCue, optional vitamin C)? Provide lab capacity, cold-chain SOPs, assay turnaround, QC, and per-assay sample sizes.
response.answer: Local labs can perform DBS CRP and HemoCue assays, with cold-chain SOPs in place, but optional vitamin C assays may require external labs. Turnaround times vary, and QC protocols are essential. Sample sizes per assay depend on lab capacity.

results.title: Glossary
results.content: | A milder form of familial adenomatous polyposis, a genetic disease causing digestive-tract polyps and increased risk of cancer. Abnormal cells are found in the glandular tissue of certain internal organs (i.e. the uterus, cervix, lung, pancreas, and colon) and may become cancer. | An allogeneic stem cell transplant uses stem cells from a well-matched donor, usually to treat a hematological (blood) cancer. Symptoms and diseases are treated with drugs, radiation, surgery, and other clinically tested means. | Von Hippel-Lindau, a genetic mutation associated with renal cell carcinoma (kidney cancer). | A rare inherited VHL mutation that affects every cell in the body, causing non-cancerous and cancerous growths, especially kidney cancer of a hard-to-treat type. | Waldenström macroglobulinemia is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in which the cancer cells produce an abnormal protein known as a macroglobulin. | ZMCs (zinc metallochaperones) are drugs that "escort" zinc into cancer cells to normalize mutated p53 genes.
